en.title: Taylor Sheridan Isn't Flattered By Hollywood's 'Yellowstone' Copycats
en.summary: Despite a wave of imitators, the creator of 'Yellowstone' isn't feeling the love. He explains why Hollywood's attempts to replicate his success miss the mark.
en.body:
Hollywood has been scrambling to bottle the lightning that is **Taylor Sheridan**'s **Yellowstone**. The sprawling Western drama has spawned a universe of prequels and spin-offs, and its immense success has inevitably led to a parade of imitators eager to capture a slice of its massive audience. You might think the man behind it all, **Taylor Sheridan**, would see these copycats as a badge of honor, a testament to his groundbreaking work. However, the reality is far from flattering for the prolific showrunner.

Sheridan himself has been quite clear about his feelings. In a 2022 interview with Variety, he expressed a distinct lack of flattery when discussing Hollywood's attempts to replicate **Yellowstone**'s success. He didn't believe these imitators were driven by an appreciation for the show's quality or narrative depth. Instead, he pinpointed the undeniable viewership numbers as the primary motivator. "I don't know that it's flattering, because I don't think they're doing it because 'Yellowstone' is good. They're doing it because 15 million people watch ['Yellowstone']. And they're like: 'A lot of people watch Westerns. Let's make Westerns.'"

## The Sheridan Empire's Unmatched Appeal

Despite Sheridan's reservations about the motivations behind the trend, the industry's gamble on Westerns and ranch-centric narratives has proven correct – at least when **Taylor Sheridan** is involved. His own slate of shows continues to dominate the streaming landscape, showcasing an undeniable audience appetite for his specific brand of storytelling. The Paramount+ series **Landman**, for instance, made a significant splash in the first half of 2026, accumulating an impressive 12.4 billion viewing minutes and securing its spot as the fourth most-streamed original series for that period. Furthermore, the 2025-26 television season saw a remarkable three **Sheridan**-produced shows – **Lawmen: Bass Reeves**, **Landman**, and **The Madison** – break into the coveted top 25 most-watched series, underscoring his unparalleled ability to connect with viewers.

## What This Means for Fans

For dedicated fans of **Taylor Sheridan**'s work, this sentiment from the creator himself adds another layer to their appreciation. It highlights that the magic of **Yellowstone**, **1883**, **1923**, and his other critically acclaimed series isn't just about the genre; it's about his unique vision, his commitment to authentic storytelling, and his deep understanding of the American West. While other networks might be chasing ratings with surface-level imitations, **Sheridan** continues to deliver rich, character-driven narratives that resonate deeply. This distinction is crucial for viewers who crave substance over spectacle, and it solidifies his position as a master storyteller whose influence is undeniable, even if he remains unmoved by the mimicry.

## What's Next

While **Taylor Sheridan** focuses on his expanding universe and upcoming projects, fans can anticipate more installments of his existing hit series. The exact release dates for future seasons of **1923** and the continuation of **Lawmen: Bass Reeves** have not yet been announced, but the continued success of **Landman** suggests further exploration of that world is likely. Viewers eager for more of Sheridan's signature style will be watching closely for any updates on his expanding slate of television and film projects.

content_raw: You might think Taylor Sheridan looks at the parade of Yellowstone copycats and considers it a compliment. However, this is not the case.
